\emph{Find the length of the curve.}
\begin{enumerate}
\item $y=\left(4-x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}\right)^{\nicefrac{3}{2}}$ from $x=0$
to $x=8$.
\end{enumerate}
$y'=-\frac{3}{2}x^{-\nicefrac{1}{3}}\frac{2}{3}\left(4-x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}\right)^{\nicefrac{1}{2}}=-\frac{\left(4-x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}\right)^{\nicefrac{1}{2}}}{x^{\nicefrac{1}{3}}}$
by the chain rule, and \\
$\left(y'\right)^{2}=\left(-\frac{\left(4-x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}\right)^{\nicefrac{1}{2}}}{x^{\nicefrac{1}{3}}}\right)^{2}=\frac{4-x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}}{x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}}$.

So then 
\begin{eqnarray*}
{\displaystyle \int_{0}^{8}\sqrt{1+\left(y'\right)^{2}}} & = & \int_{0}^{8}\sqrt{1+\frac{4-x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}}{x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}}}\,dx\\
 & = & \int_{0}^{8}\sqrt{\frac{x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}+4-x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}}{x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}}}\,dx\\
 & = & \int_{0}^{8}\sqrt{\frac{4}{x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}}}\,dx=\int_{0}^{8}2x^{-\nicefrac{1}{3}}\,dx\\
 & = & \frac{2}{\nicefrac{2}{3}}x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}|_{0}^{8}=3x^{\nicefrac{2}{3}}|_{0}^{8}=12-0=12
\end{eqnarray*}
\vspace{2cm}

\emph{Find the derivative using logarithmic differentiation.}

$\frac{d}{dx}\ln f(x)=\frac{1}{f(x)}f'(x)\mbox{ (by the chain rule)}\Rightarrow f'(x)=f(x)\frac{d}{dx}\left[\ln f(x)\right]$
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $f(x)=x^{\ln x}$
\end{enumerate}
So, $\ln\left(f(x)\right)=\ln\left(x^{\ln x}\right)=\ln(x)\ln(x)$
($\ln x^{y}=y\cdot\ln x$), and 
\begin{eqnarray*}
f'(x) & = & x^{\ln x}\frac{d}{dx}\left[\ln\left(x^{\ln x}\right)\right]\\
 & = & x^{\ln x}\left[\frac{1}{x}\ln(x)+\frac{1}{x}\ln(x)\right]\\
 & = & \frac{2x^{\ln x}\ln(x)}{x}=2x^{\ln x-1}\ln x\mbox{.}
\end{eqnarray*}

It is usually preferable to combine the variables when possible. This
is why the text has the answer in the last form.
